no figure may be presented as a market rate or a guaranteed outcome; only the structure and its documented inputs are shown
every building-dependent quantity must ride into the proposal as a labelled assumption with a survey contingency
reference material, measurements and sample reports may only be shared with permission and with customer and guest data removed
a tier whose promised response cannot be funded or staffed at its price has to be changed rather than sold
competing against a one-time installation quote pushes the monthly price toward a number the service cannot be delivered for
edges.resolution_rule: hold the cost-built floor: if the buyer wants the lower figure, change the tier or the scope openly and reprice from the same structure, or lose the deal; never discount into a price the serviceability check fails

edges.why_related: property owners sometimes want resident contact data, marketing access or visibility into resident traffic as part of the deal
edges.resolution_rule: the privacy commitment wins without exception: no interception and no resale; any collection must be disclosed, consented and owned by the property under rules verified in that jurisdiction, and the deal is declined if that is refused

edges.why_related: a venue that trades at night needs cover the standard tier does not include, which pressures the ladder toward bespoke exceptions
edges.resolution_rule: sell the rung that matches the trading hours or a written, priced extension of hours; never promise out-of-hours response verbally inside a business-hours tier

edges.why_related: an easy exit and a fronted-equipment model pull against each other, since the venue can leave before the cost is recovered
edges.resolution_rule: match the recovery period to the term; if the buyer requires a short or freely cancellable term, switch to customer-purchased equipment or a stated buyout figure computed from the remaining balance, never a hidden penalty

edges.why_related: a partner's pitch may promise coverage, pricing or response the provider would never claim in its own name
edges.resolution_rule: the provider's claim discipline governs anything said in its name: brief partners in writing, correct the collateral, and reset the venue's expectation in the first meeting even when that costs the referral

edges.why_related: buyers want one firm number today while the facts that decide the number are still unmeasured
edges.resolution_rule: quote the structure plus a conditional range tied to a named assumption list and a survey contingency; never convert an assumption into a fixed promise to win the meeting

edges.why_related: what the venue actually depends on determines which value story is load-bearing and how strong the case for a monthly fee is
adoptable existing equipment shrinks the amount that must be fronted or financed and changes which funding option fits
building conditions, access constraints and travel distance drive the onsite hours a site will consume every year
where a lead came from predicts how it screens: dealer and integrator referrals usually arrive with dependence established, cold property leads often fail on consent
establish what exists and who controls it first, then list what only a survey can settle
the class-shaped offer is assembled before the proposal is written so the document carries the right coverage basis and privacy wording
measured support hours and travel from live sites retune the components of the rate structure for the next quote
a class or channel that keeps producing declines is telling the provider its targeting is wrong
survey findings that contradict a signed assumption feed back into the standard assumption list used on the next quote
both are multi-unit residential-style buildings priced against doors and corridors, with per-unit coverage expectations and heavy consent and privacy considerations

conflict_axes.name: recurring_accountability_vs_upfront_cash
conflict_axes.description: A one-time installation pays immediately and closes; a subscription pays slowly and obliges the provider for years, and a young business needs the cash the first model gives it.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: sell the subscription as the product and price installation to cover its own cost, taking installation-only work honestly and separately when the buyer genuinely wants nothing more

conflict_axes.name: productized_tiers_vs_venue_specific_fit
conflict_axes.description: A short ladder of tiers makes the offer repeatable and priceable, but every venue has a genuine need that sits between two rungs.
poles: shape the agreement to the venue
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: keep the rungs fixed and express the difference as a written, priced option rather than a new bespoke scope; if the same option recurs, promote it into the ladder

conflict_axes.name: guest_amenity_story_vs_operations_dependence_story
conflict_axes.description: Guest coverage is the visible, emotionally easy story; operations dependence is the one that justifies a permanent monthly charge, and leading with the wrong one loses or mis-sizes the deal.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let the dependency inventory decide which leads for this venue, and use the other as support rather than telling both stories at equal volume

conflict_axes.name: customer_owned_hardware_vs_provider_funded_hardware
conflict_axes.description: Customer purchase protects the provider's cash and simplifies the exit; provider funding removes the upfront barrier but converts equipment into an unrecovered balance if the venue leaves.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: choose per deal against the term and the venue's stability, and always write ownership, recovery and end-of-term treatment into the proposal

conflict_axes.name: speed_to_quote_vs_survey_dependent_certainty
conflict_axes.description: Deals are often won by whoever answers first, but the facts that decide access-point count, cabling and price cannot be known without visiting the building.
poles: answer fast with a firm number
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: answer fast with the structure, an explicit assumption list and a conditional range, and reserve the firm figure for after the survey

conflict_axes.name: portal_data_value_vs_guest_privacy
conflict_axes.description: Sign-in pages can collect contact details that venues value commercially, and vendors market that capability, but the people typing them in are guests and residents who deserve disclosure and restraint.
poles: capture and use guest contact data
collect the minimum and disclose it plainly
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: no interception and no resale ever; collection only for a stated venue purpose, disclosed on the page, owned by the venue, and checked against current local rules

conflict_axes.name: term_security_vs_customer_exit_freedom
conflict_axes.description: A longer committed term secures recovery and revenue; an easy exit builds trust and sells better, especially to owners who have been trapped before.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: set the term by what must be recovered, state notice and buyout in plain language, and never use credentials, configuration or documentation as leverage to prevent leaving

conflict_axes.name: price_competitiveness_vs_serviceable_margin
conflict_axes.description: Winning against a cheaper bid pulls the monthly figure down while the promised response, spares and travel keep costing what they cost.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: reprice by changing scope or tier in the open, and decline rather than sell a response the price cannot fund

conflict_axes.name: single_accountable_party_vs_carrier_boundary
conflict_axes.description: Venues want one company to blame for anything that looks like the internet, while the circuit belongs to a carrier the provider does not control.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: own triage and communication across the whole path while holding remedies and credits to the managed side, and write both halves into the agreement

conflict_axes.name: broad_venue_reach_vs_route_density
conflict_axes.description: Accepting every venue class across a wide area grows revenue fastest, but scattered sites destroy response times and load the week with driving.
conflict_axes.resolution_hint: let the serviceability check price or refuse distance honestly, and treat clusters of one class in one area as the growth path rather than one-off distant sites

edge_cases.description: The venue's internet circuit is inadequate or heavily oversubscribed, and every complaint is being blamed on the Wi-Fi
edge_cases.trigger: discovery or early monitoring shows the bottleneck sits on the carrier side of the demarcation point
edge_cases.mitigation: establish the circuit facts before quoting, state the boundary in writing, make the offer conditional on a circuit capable of the expected load, and decline the deal if the venue wants the wireless network to fix a carrier problem

edge_cases.description: A buyer demands a guaranteed uptime or speed figure before anyone has surveyed the building
edge_cases.trigger: a competitor has quoted a number, or the buyer wants certainty written into the contract at first meeting
edge_cases.mitigation: explain the mechanism and what will be measured, offer conditional language plus a post-survey commitment, and decline to sign a figure the building has not been shown to support

edge_cases.description: The landlord or building owner controls risers, roof and common areas and will not give written consent
edge_cases.trigger: a multi-tenant or multi-dwelling deal needs access to shared infrastructure the venue does not control
edge_cases.mitigation: obtain written consent as a precondition of the quote, rescope to what can be done inside the tenant's own space, or decline; never begin shared-space work on a verbal assurance

edge_cases.description: A branded venue's franchisor specifies particular equipment, configuration or a vendor list
edge_cases.trigger: the venue carries a hospitality or food-service brand with a technology standard
edge_cases.mitigation: read the current brand specification before quoting, reshape the offer to comply or state plainly that it does not, and never claim brand compliance that has not been verified against the document

edge_cases.description: The venue asks the provider to capture guest emails and phone numbers at sign-in and feed them to a marketing platform
edge_cases.trigger: a marketing consultant or a vendor has told the owner that guest data is the real value of guest Wi-Fi
edge_cases.mitigation: refuse interception and any resale outright; allow only disclosed, consented, venue-owned collection with the notice text agreed in advance and the applicable privacy rules verified in that jurisdiction

edge_cases.description: A prospect wants the installation only and no monthly service at all
edge_cases.trigger: a buyer with capital, an internal technical contact, or an aversion to subscriptions
edge_cases.mitigation: quote the installation honestly with documentation and credential handover, price it to cover its own cost, and decline or defer rather than attaching a management fee to work that will not be performed

edge_cases.description: The only administrative credentials for the existing network are held by a former employee or an unreachable acquaintance
edge_cases.trigger: the incumbent audit cannot produce access or documentation for equipment that must be adopted or replaced
edge_cases.mitigation: make credential recovery or factory reset and rebuild an explicit, priced line in the proposal, and do not offer an installation date until ownership of the equipment is confirmed

edge_cases.description: A small multi-site operator wants one monthly figure covering venues of very different sizes and conditions
edge_cases.trigger: a group of restaurants or shops under one owner asks for portfolio pricing
edge_cases.mitigation: price each site from the same structure and present the portfolio as the sum with any group treatment shown explicitly, so no site is silently subsidising another into a loss

edge_cases.description: A competitor bids far below the provider's structure for what looks like the same service
edge_cases.trigger: a price-led bid arrives late in the deal, often with no scope document
edge_cases.mitigation: compare contents side by side without characterising the competitor, offer a lower rung honestly if the buyer wants less service, and be willing to lose the deal rather than sell an unfundable response

edge_cases.description: The venue sits far outside the service radius or can only be worked on outside its trading hours
edge_cases.trigger: a distant referral or a venue that trades continuously and cannot take an install window
edge_cases.mitigation: price travel and out-of-hours work explicitly, consider a local partner, and decline where the response promise cannot be met at any price the buyer will accept

edge_cases.description: Equipment pricing, lead time or model availability changes between quote and signature
edge_cases.trigger: a supply constraint, a price increase or an end-of-life notice from the vendor
edge_cases.mitigation: attach a validity window to every quote, re-verify supplier pricing and availability before signature, and reissue rather than absorbing a cost the structure never carried

edge_cases.description: The venue changes hands or closes partway through the term with equipment cost unrecovered
edge_cases.trigger: a sale of the business, a lease ending, or a seasonal venue that does not reopen
edge_cases.mitigation: write transfer, buyout and equipment retrieval into the agreement from the start, offer the new owner the same terms, and hand over credentials, configuration and documentation regardless of how the relationship ends

workflow.action: Fix the service definition before anything is quoted
workflow.description: State the bundled components, the accountable outcome and the standing monthly obligation in one page the whole business sells from
workflow.gate: the statement names the three components, the outcome, and at least three activities performed every month when nothing is broken

workflow.action: Choose and characterise the venue classes to serve
workflow.description: Record the signing role, demand trigger, footprint driver, consent requirement and disqualifier for each class the provider will pursue
workflow.gate: every served class has all five attributes recorded and no class is on the list without a reachable buyer

workflow.action: Set the selling constraints before any collateral exists
workflow.description: Write the guest and resident privacy commitments and the claim discipline that bounds every conversation and document
workflow.artifact: selling constraints sheet covering privacy commitments and permitted claims
workflow.gate: the no-interception and no-resale commitments, the disclosure-first collection rule and the banned-claim list exist in writing before a pitch is delivered

workflow.action: Settle the obligation classes and who holds each
workflow.description: Name the licensing, code, consent, insurance and privacy-notice classes attached to install-plus-manage work and assign each a holder
workflow.artifact: obligation register with holders and verification notes
workflow.gate: every class is held in-house, subcontracted to a licensed trade, or assigned to the venue, and each carries a verify-locally note

workflow.action: Run venue discovery on the specific site
workflow.description: Inventory the network-dependent systems and their consequences with the staff who use them, and confirm the list back to the venue
workflow.artifact: operations dependency inventory confirmed by the venue
workflow.gate: each system has its vendor, its connection today and the venue's own stated consequence, and the venue has agreed the list is accurate

workflow.action: Audit the incumbent arrangement and list the survey-pending facts
workflow.description: Record existing equipment, ownership, credentials and contracts, then write down everything about the building that only a survey can settle
workflow.artifact: incumbent audit plus a labelled assumption list
workflow.gate: credential and ownership state is known and every building-dependent quantity is marked survey-pending with its assumption

workflow.action: Define the monthly scope and the tier ladder
workflow.description: Write the inclusions, the exclusions, the change allowance, the support hours and the few dimensions along which tiers differ
workflow.gate: nothing in the tier exists only in conversation, and each rung states hours, response expectation and change allowance

workflow.description: Fix where the carrier's service ends, what the managed scope covers, which applications belong to their vendors, and what triage the provider performs across the line
workflow.gate: the demarcation point is identified and the out-of-boundary triage promise is stated with the tier it belongs to

workflow.action: Build the price from its components and choose the equipment funding model
workflow.description: Assemble per-site and per-device components from held cost documents, apply the modifiers, and pick purchase, amortised or provider-owned equipment
workflow.artifact: quote worksheet with component trace and funding choice
workflow.gate: every component traces to a cost document, the quote carries a validity window, and equipment ownership and recovery are decided

workflow.action: Run the serviceability and capacity check
workflow.description: Estimate monthly effort, travel and expected support contacts against the quoted price and against current portfolio capacity
workflow.gate: the site can be served at the quoted price and tier without breaking the response promised to existing customers, or the tier and price are changed

workflow.action: Shape the offer to the venue class and screen the deal
workflow.description: Apply the class-specific shaping, then run the written go, conditional or no-go screen and record the reason either way
workflow.artifact: venue-shaped offer draft with a recorded fit decision
workflow.gate: no disqualifier is unaddressed, every conditional yes names its condition, and any decline records its reason

workflow.action: Assemble the signable proposal and hand off to design
workflow.description: Produce the one document carrying scope, tier, conditional quantities, price structure, exclusions, equipment ownership, term and exit, boundary, privacy commitments and open permissions
workflow.artifact: signable proposal with assumption list and open-permission list
workflow.gate: every required element is present, every pending fact is labelled, and the assumption and permission lists travel with the deal into design and deployment

dominance_rules.rule: The guest and resident privacy commitment dominates any revenue idea that depends on their data
dominance_rules.rationale: interception or resale of the data of people who did not choose the provider is a breach of trust that no monthly fee can repair, and it is the boundary this business is built on
dominance_rules.trigger: a venue, a partner or a vendor proposes collecting, inspecting or monetizing guest traffic or identifiers
dominance_rules.action: refuse interception and resale outright, allow only disclosed and consented venue-owned collection verified against current local rules, and decline the deal if that is not acceptable

dominance_rules.rule: Survey-pending facts dominate the desire to give a firm number today
dominance_rules.rationale: a promise made against an unmeasured building becomes an unfunded obligation the moment the survey disagrees
dominance_rules.trigger: a buyer presses for a fixed price, access-point count or coverage guarantee before the site has been surveyed
dominance_rules.action: give the structure, a conditional range and the assumption list with its contingency, and hold the firm figure until measurement

dominance_rules.rationale: an exaggerated promise wins one deal and loses the account, the reference and the referral chain behind it
dominance_rules.trigger: a competitor quotes a performance figure or a guarantee the provider cannot evidence
dominance_rules.action: state what can be evidenced, explain what the competitor's number would require, and accept losing the deal rather than matching an unsupportable claim

dominance_rules.rule: Permission and licensing obligations dominate the sale
dominance_rules.rationale: work that cannot be lawfully or contractually performed is worse than no work: it stalls, exposes the provider and damages the venue relationship
dominance_rules.trigger: an obligation class is unresolved, unverified or belongs to a party that has not consented in writing
dominance_rules.action: hold the deal at a conditional state until the class has a holder and written consent, and decline if it cannot be resolved

dominance_rules.rationale: a site sold below what its service costs damages every existing customer by consuming the capacity their response promise depends on
dominance_rules.trigger: the serviceability check fails at the quoted tier and price
dominance_rules.action: change the tier, price the hours and travel honestly, or decline the site rather than adding it to the book

dominance_rules.rule: The written scope dominates any verbal expectation
dominance_rules.rationale: everything not written becomes a dispute at the worst possible moment, which is during an outage
dominance_rules.trigger: a request or an assurance exists in conversation but not in the agreement
dominance_rules.action: put it in the scope as an inclusion or an exclusion before signature, and treat unwritten assurances as not sold

dominance_rules.rule: The venue's ownership of its own network dominates any retention tactic
dominance_rules.rationale: holding credentials, configuration or documentation hostage is coercion, and it is also the fastest way to earn a reputation that ends referrals
dominance_rules.trigger: a customer gives notice, disputes an invoice or asks for administrative access
dominance_rules.action: hand over credentials, current configuration and documentation for venue-owned equipment as written, and settle any commercial dispute separately

dominance_rules.rule: Honest product framing dominates the temptation to attach a fee to work not performed
dominance_rules.rationale: a management fee for services not rendered is the failure mode that discredits the entire managed-service category
dominance_rules.trigger: a buyer wants only an installation, or a quiet site tempts the provider to let monitoring lapse while billing continues
dominance_rules.action: sell installation as installation, and either perform every activity the subscription names or reduce the subscription to what is actually performed

dominance_rules.rule: The stated demarcation dominates blame during an outage
dominance_rules.rationale: accountability that is undefined defaults to the last party the venue spoke to, which is usually the provider
dominance_rules.trigger: an outage originates with the carrier, a vendor application or a venue-owned device
dominance_rules.action: run triage, communicate the finding, act on the third party where the tier says so, and apply remedies only to the managed side of the line

dominance_rules.rule: Unpressured understanding dominates the urge to close today, and most of all with buyers least able to evaluate the offer
dominance_rules.rationale: a venue owner with no technical staff cannot judge coverage claims or scope wording under time pressure, and a signature obtained that way produces a disappointed customer, a refund argument and a lost reference
dominance_rules.trigger: a buyer is being asked to decide immediately, is unfamiliar with the technology, or is under external pressure such as a brand inspection or a bad review cycle
dominance_rules.action: slow down: give the exclusions and the assumption list in plain language, answer what the fee does not cover, allow time to read, and never attach an invented deadline or an expiring discount to the decision

anti_rework_rules.rule: Write the monthly scope before any price is calculated
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a fee that has to be renegotiated once the work it must fund is finally written down

anti_rework_rules.rule: Complete the operations dependency inventory before choosing which value story leads
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a pitch aimed at guest amenity for a venue whose real pain is transaction systems, and the re-scoping that follows

anti_rework_rules.rule: Set the privacy commitments and claim limits before producing collateral or a partner brief
anti_rework_rules.prevents: recalling published material and correcting expectations already set with venues and partners

anti_rework_rules.rule: Mark every building-dependent quantity survey-pending before it appears in a quote
anti_rework_rules.prevents: an unfunded promise that has to be absorbed or renegotiated once the survey disagrees

anti_rework_rules.rule: Draw the carrier, managed-network and application boundary before promising a support path
anti_rework_rules.prevents: inheriting carrier and vendor failures as service obligations that were never priced

anti_rework_rules.rule: Decide the equipment funding model before setting the term
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a term too short to recover fronted equipment, which can only be fixed by a renegotiation the customer resents

anti_rework_rules.rule: Run the serviceability and capacity check before signing a tier
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a book of sites whose promised response cannot be delivered, which then churns and consumes the reputation that sold it

anti_rework_rules.rule: Obtain written landlord, franchisor and property consent before offering an installation date
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a scheduled crew turned away at the door and a rebuild of the project timeline

anti_rework_rules.rule: Build the tier ladder before customising for any individual deal
anti_rework_rules.prevents: a portfolio of bespoke agreements that cannot be priced, staffed, compared or renewed consistently

iteration_protocol.trigger: the survey contradicts an assumption the quote relied on
iteration_protocol.action: invoke the stated contingency, reprice or rescope from the same structure, and reissue before installation begins

iteration_protocol.trigger: supplier licence, equipment or insurance costs change
iteration_protocol.action: recompute the affected price components, revisit tier margins and refresh the quote validity window

iteration_protocol.trigger: measured support load or travel time per site diverges from what the tier assumed
iteration_protocol.action: retune the effort estimates, adjust the tier contents or the price for that venue type, and re-test portfolio capacity before selling more of it

iteration_protocol.trigger: a venue asks to change what the sign-in page collects, or privacy rules in its jurisdiction change
iteration_protocol.action: restate the privacy commitment, rewrite the disclosure text with the venue, verify current local rules and refuse anything the commitment forbids

iteration_protocol.trigger: the same out-of-scope request recurs across several venues
iteration_protocol.action: promote it into a tier or price it as a standard option instead of absorbing it deal by deal

iteration_protocol.trigger: a venue class or a partner channel keeps failing the fit screen
iteration_protocol.action: revise the class targeting or re-brief the partner in writing, and adjust the referral terms or stop taking those leads

iteration_protocol.trigger: a claim in circulation can no longer be evidenced, or a reference customer withdraws permission
iteration_protocol.action: withdraw the claim or asset, replace it with something currently measurable, and check where else it was used

iteration_protocol.trigger: cancellations cluster around a term mechanic, an equipment model or an ownership transfer
iteration_protocol.action: revisit term, notice and buyout structure and the funding model behind it, then update the proposal template

priority_rationale: The framing units come first because nothing can be priced, pitched or declined before the service being sold, the venue classes worth serving, the privacy and claim boundaries and the permission obligations are settled; discovery of the venue's dependence, its incumbent arrangement and its unmeasured site facts must precede any offer architecture, since scope, price, equipment funding and term all consume those facts; the venue-shaping and positioning units then apply the architecture to a specific class and a specific competitor situation; and the fit screen and the proposal gate come last because they compose everything upstream into a decision to proceed and a document that can be signed and handed to design without ambiguity.
